Well that's a bit of title butchery. No, breeder reactors do not provide unlimited energy or anything even remotely close to it. The nuclear process of a breeder reactor converts a currently unused part of the fuel into usable nuclear material - fissile material. In particular uranium/thorium are converted into plutonium - and in greater quantities than originally input. However, that original source material is gone and the produced material will be consumed in future reactions. The net result is just an increase in productivity. The article mentions they're aiming for an increase of about 70% efficiency.

Well that's cool - a free 70% increase in productivity. Why aren't all reactors breeders? Because it's not free. The reactors are vastly more complex, expensive, and unstable. The coolant in breeder reactors is liquid sodium. This video demonstrates the effect between water and sodium. It even goes boom when exposed to air. And we're just getting started. The extra fun part about breeder reactors is what was already mentioned - that fissile material. It's plutonium, plutonium 239 in particular. That plutonium is weapons grade and be directly used in the development of nuclear weapons. Think about the implications of this. On top of having increasingly temperamental nuclear plants (when we're having a hard enough time as is) with systems that become incredibly violent when exposed to water or air, you'd also need what would be military scale defense of the entire operation as the extra fissile material is the key ingredient for nuclear weapons.

If India is indeed going through with this, I'd expect the goal is to provide power while also further supplementing their nuclear arsenal. India is not a signatory of the nuclear non-proliferation treaty.
